mcqs.q: Telehealth is defined as the use of electronic information & telecommunications to support:
opts: Long-distance clinical care, education, public health and administration
mcqs.explain: Telehealth supports long-distance clinical health care, patient/professional education, public health and health administration.

mcqs.q: Telemedicine specifically refers to:
opts: Exchanging medical information from one site to another to improve health status
mcqs.explain: Telemedicine is the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another via electronic communications to improve patients' health status.

mcqs.q: A goal of telemedicine is:
opts: Timely, high-quality remote care with high patient satisfaction and less time lost from work
mcqs.explain: Goals: provide timely, high-quality care remotely, and achieve high satisfaction through better access to specialty care and less time lost from work.

mcqs.q: Which communication mode is asynchronous, allows photo attachment and has an audit trail?
mcqs.explain: Portal secure messaging is asynchronous, can attach photos, use templates and has an audit trail, but is less personal and often not linked to the EHR.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of the TELEPHONE communication mode is that it is:
mcqs.explain: Telephone is widely available, simple and inexpensive, but it is not asynchronous, is unstructured and has no audit trail.

mcqs.q: The 'store-and-forward' transmission mode is best described as:
mcqs.explain: Store-and-forward saves images/videos and sends them later (e.g. a rash photo forwarded to a dermatologist) — asynchronous communication.

mcqs.q: Which transmission mode is SYNCHRONOUS, often using two-way interactive television?
mcqs.explain: Real-time telemedicine has a specialist view live video and discuss the case (synchronous), often via two-way interactive televisions.

mcqs.q: Monitoring patients at home or in a nursing home for health information is:
mcqs.explain: Remote monitoring is a technique to monitor patients at home, in a nursing home or hospital for personal health information or disease management.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised CATEGORY of telemedicine?
mcqs.explain: Categories include teleradiology, teledermatology, telecardiology, telepathology, telesurgery, telepsychiatry, teleneurology, teleophthalmology and telepharmacy.

mcqs.q: Traditional telemedicine programs typically consist of:
opts: A central medical hub with several rural 'spokes'
A single doctor with no network
mcqs.explain: Most traditional programs consist of a central medical hub and several rural spokes, improving access in rural/underserved areas including prisons.

mcqs.q: 'Telerounding' was developed mainly to address:
opts: The shortage of physicians and nurses
mcqs.explain: Telerounding helps address the shortage of physicians and nurses, enabling providers to conduct patient rounds remotely (e.g. robot rounds, e-ICU).

mcqs.q: Health Buddy, a home-monitoring system, covers approximately:
opts: 45 disease protocols with daily interactive questions
mcqs.explain: Health Buddy sends data via phone lines, comes with decision-support software, covers 45 disease protocols and asks patients questions daily.

mcqs.q: A feature of HoneyWell HomMed is that it:
opts: Provides voice messages in multiple languages and (via LifeStream Connect) interfaces with EHRs
mcqs.explain: HomMed provides voice messages in multiple languages, optional digital scale/BP/oximetry/glucometer, transmits via phone lines, and LifeStream Connect interfaces with EHRs.

mcqs.q: Telemanagement programs are interactive and include patient education for issues such as:
mcqs.explain: Telemanagement programs are interactive and include patient education for issues such as drug compliance, often interfacing with an EHR.

mcqs.q: Which is a telehealth organization?
mcqs.explain: Telehealth organizations include the Office for the Advancement of Telehealth (OAT) and the American Telemedicine Association (ATA).

mcqs.q: Which is a BARRIER to telemedicine?
opts: Limited reimbursement and bandwidth issues (especially rural)
mcqs.explain: Barriers include limited reimbursement, slow clinical acceptance, limited research/ROI, high cost, bandwidth issues (rural), lack of standards and fear of malpractice.

mcqs.q: Teledentistry is best defined as:
opts: A combination of telecommunications and dentistry exchanging clinical information and images over distance
mcqs.explain: Teledentistry combines telecommunications and dentistry, exchanging clinical information and images over remote distances for dental consultation and treatment planning.

mcqs.q: The basis of modern teledentistry systems is the:
mcqs.explain: The Internet is the basis of modern systems of teledentistry.

mcqs.q: The two methods of teleconsultation in dentistry are:
mcqs.explain: Methods of teleconsultation in dentistry are real-time consultation and the store-and-forward method.

mcqs.q: Teledentistry holds promise for which dental disciplines?
opts: Endodontics, orthodontics, oral surgery and paediatric dentistry
mcqs.explain: Teledentistry has promising benefits for endodontics, orthodontics, oral surgery and paediatric dentistry, improving access in rural/underserved areas.

mcqs.q: A key ethical/legal concern in teledentistry is:
opts: Confidentiality of records and possible interception of transmitted information
mcqs.explain: Concerns about confidentiality arise from transferring records; patients should be told their information is transmitted electronically and may be intercepted despite security.

mcqs.q: According to the conclusion, the barriers to telemedicine are largely:
opts: Financial — high setup cost and lack of reimbursement
mcqs.explain: The barriers are largely financial, due to the high cost to set up systems and the lack of reimbursement, though prices are dropping.

saqs.a: Telehealth = the use of electronic information & telecommunications to support long-distance clinical care, education, public health and administration. Telemedicine = the exchange of medical information from one site to another via electronic communications to improve a patient's health status.

saqs.q: List and describe the three transmission modes of telemedicine.
saqs.a: Store-and-forward — images/videos saved and sent later (asynchronous). Real-time — live video discussion (synchronous, two-way TV). Remote monitoring — monitoring patients at home/nursing home/hospital.

saqs.q: Compare the three telemedicine communication modes.
saqs.a: Portal messaging — asynchronous, photos, audit trail, but impersonal/not EHR-linked. Telephone — simple & cheap, but unstructured with no audit trail. Audio-video — maximal input (review x-rays) & personal, but most expensive in network/hardware.
Traditional (central hub with rural spokes), telerounding (remote rounds; robot/e-ICU), and telehomecare & telemanagement (e.g. Health Buddy, HoneyWell HomMed).

saqs.q: Define teledentistry and state its methods.
saqs.a: Teledentistry = a combination of telecommunications and dentistry, exchanging clinical information and images over distance for consultation and treatment planning. Methods: real-time consultation and store-and-forward (Internet-based).
Limited reimbursement, slow clinical acceptance, limited research/ROI, high cost, bandwidth issues (rural), lack of standards, and fear of malpractice.
